question: In 2023, the Total Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) for elementary schools in India stood at _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**100.1%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2023, the Total Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) for elementary schools in India was 100.1.
 
• The GER is a statistical measure used in the education sector to determine the number of students enrolled in a particular level of education, regardless of age, expressed as a percentage of the population of the age group that officially corresponds to the same level of education.
 
• India's GER of 100.1 indicates that the number of students enrolled at the elementary level is equivalent to the population of the age group that should be at this level, suggesting near-universal enrollment.
 
• This metric reflects the government's ongoing efforts to improve access to elementary education across the country.
 
• It is a key indicator used by policymakers to assess the reach and inclusiveness of the education system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER):**

 
 
• GER is an important education index that measures total enrollment in a specific level of education.
 
• It can exceed 100% when there are significant numbers of students enrolled who are older or younger than the official age group for that level of education.
 
• GER is used to gauge the level of participation in education.
 
 
 
• **Net Enrollment Ratio (NER):**
 
 
• NER is a more precise measure than GER as it only includes students of the official age group for a given level of education.
 
• NER helps in understanding the extent to which the education system is retaining students within the official age brackets.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act:**
 
 
• Enacted in 2009, the RTE Act in India mandates free and compulsory education for children between the ages of 6 and 14.
 
• It aims to improve enrollment rates, reduce dropout rates, and ensure quality education.
 
 
 
• **Mid-Day Meal Scheme:**
 
 
• This scheme provides free lunches to children in primary and upper primary classes in government and government-aided schools.
 
• It aims to enhance enrollment, retention, and attendance while simultaneously improving nutritional levels among children.
